import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.19

by Yu. G. Kleiman

Which of the following properties of (soluble) varieties of groups are equivalent to one
another:

1) to satisfy the minimum condition for subvarieties;

2) to have at most countably many subvarieties;

3) to have no infinite independent system of identities?

An *identity* (law) is a word $w$ in the free group on the variables $x_0, x_1, \dots$; a group
$G$ *satisfies* $w$ if $w$ evaluates to $1$ under every substitution of elements of $G$ for the
variables. A *variety of groups* is the class of all groups satisfying a given set of
identities, and a *subvariety* of a variety $\mathfrak{V}$ is a variety contained in
$\mathfrak{V}$. A set $S$ of identities is *independent in* $\mathfrak{V}$ if no $w \in S$ is a
consequence of $S \setminus \{w\}$ modulo the identities of $\mathfrak{V}$, i.e. for every
$w \in S$ some group in $\mathfrak{V}$ satisfies all identities of $S \setminus \{w\}$ but
not $w$. A variety is *soluble* if all of its groups are soluble.

Every variety is determined by its groups of countable cardinality (it is determined by its
relatively free group of countable rank), so here a variety is recorded by the class of its
groups in `Type`.

The question is split into the three pairwise equivalences 1) ⇔ 2), 1) ⇔ 3) and 2) ⇔ 3),
each asked for all varieties of groups and, as a variant, for all soluble varieties of groups.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/
namespace Kourovka.«8.19»

blocks.code:
def IsLaw (w : FreeGroup ℕ) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f w = 1
blocks.docstring:
A word `w` in the free group on the variables `x₀, x₁, …` is a *law* (identity) of the
group `G` if it evaluates to `1` under every substitution of elements of `G` for the
variables.

justification.closest_existing_considered: FreeGroup.lift (used); nothing in Mathlib.GroupTheory or Mathlib.ModelTheory captures equational laws of groups.
justification.name: Kourovka.«8.19».IsLaw
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no notion of a group identity/law. Defined as: w : FreeGroup ℕ is a law of G iff FreeGroup.lift f w = 1 for every f : ℕ → G.

blocks.name: IsLaw
blocks.text:
/-- A word `w` in the free group on the variables `x₀, x₁, …` is a *law* (identity) of the

def IsLaw (w : FreeGroup ℕ) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f w = 1

structure GroupVariety where
  /-- The groups belonging to the variety. -/
  Mem : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop
  /-- The variety is the class of all groups satisfying some set `W` of laws. -/
  exists_laws :
    ∃ W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ), ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Mem G ↔ ∀ w ∈ W, IsLaw w G
blocks.docstring: A *variety of groups*: the class of all groups satisfying some set of laws.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib.ModelTheory (Language/Theory/ModelSet) — it has no equational classes and would be far less transparent; Birkhoff-style HSP-closed classes would need a Birkhoff theorem argument for faithfulness. Searched Mathlib and FormalConjecturesForMathlib for 'variet', 'IsLaw', 'equational'.
justification.name: Kourovka.«8.19».GroupVariety
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no notion of a variety of groups (or equational class). Defined as a structure: a predicate Mem on groups in Type together with a proof that Mem is the class of all groups satisfying some set W of laws (H. Neumann's definition). Comes with a PartialOrder (inclusion, so U ≤ V means U is a subvariety of V) and an OrderTop instance (the variety of all groups), plus API lemmas le_def, mem_of_subsingleton.

/-- A *variety of groups*: the class of all groups satisfying some set of laws. -/
structure GroupVariety where
  /-- The groups belonging to the variety. -/
  Mem : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop
  /-- The variety is the class of all groups satisfying some set `W` of laws. -/
  exists_laws :
    ∃ W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ), ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Mem G ↔ ∀ w ∈ W, IsLaw w G
namespace GroupVariety

blocks.code:
instance : PartialOrder GroupVariety where
  le U V := ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], U.Mem G → V.Mem G
  le_refl _ _ _ := id
  le_trans _ _ _ h₁ h₂ G _ hG := h₂ G (h₁ G hG)
  le_antisymm U V h₁ h₂ := by
    cases U
    cases V
    congr
    funext G _
    exact propext ⟨h₁ G, h₂ G⟩
blocks.docstring: Varieties are ordered by inclusion: `U ≤ V` means that `U` is a subvariety of `V`.
blocks.text:
/-- Varieties are ordered by inclusion: `U ≤ V` means that `U` is a subvariety of `V`. -/
instance : PartialOrder GroupVariety where
  le U V := ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], U.Mem G → V.Mem G
  le_refl _ _ _ := id
  le_trans _ _ _ h₁ h₂ G _ hG := h₂ G (h₁ G hG)
  le_antisymm U V h₁ h₂ := by
    cases U
    cases V
    congr
    funext G _
    exact propext ⟨h₁ G, h₂ G⟩

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem le_def (U V : GroupVariety) : U ≤ V ↔ ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], U.Mem G → V.Mem G :=
  Iff.rfl

blocks.text:
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem le_def (U V : GroupVariety) : U ≤ V ↔ ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], U.Mem G → V.Mem G :=

/-- The variety of all groups. -/
instance : OrderTop GroupVariety where
  top := { Mem := fun _ _ => True, exists_laws := ⟨∅, fun _ _ => by simp⟩ }
  le_top _ _ _ _ := trivial

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem mem_of_subsingleton (V : GroupVariety) (G : Type) [Group G] [Subsingleton G] :
    V.Mem G := by
  obtain ⟨W, hW⟩ := V.exists_laws
  exact (hW G).2 fun w _ => isLaw_of_subsingleton w G

def IsConsequence (V : GroupVariety) (S : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (w : FreeGroup ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], V.Mem G → (∀ s ∈ S, IsLaw s G) → IsLaw w G
blocks.docstring:
The word `w` is a *consequence of `S` modulo `V`*: every group in `V` in which all words
of `S` are laws also has `w` as a law.

justification.name: Kourovka.«8.19».GroupVariety.IsConsequence
justification.why_needed: 'w follows from S modulo V': every group in V in which all words of S are laws has w as a law. Needed to define independence relative to V.

blocks.name: IsConsequence
blocks.text:
/-- The word `w` is a *consequence of `S` modulo `V`*: every group in `V` in which all words
of `S` are laws also has `w` as a law. -/
def IsConsequence (V : GroupVariety) (S : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (w : FreeGroup ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], V.Mem G → (∀ s ∈ S, IsLaw s G) → IsLaw w G

blocks.code:
def IsIndependent (V : GroupVariety) (S : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) : Prop :=
  ∀ w ∈ S, ¬ V.IsConsequence (S \ {w}) w
blocks.docstring:
A set of words `S` is an *independent system of identities in `V`* if no `w ∈ S` is a
consequence of the remaining words `S \ {w}` modulo `V`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: LinearIndependent/AlgebraicIndependent are unrelated; nothing for equational independence.
justification.name: Kourovka.«8.19».GroupVariety.IsIndependent
justification.why_needed: A set S of words is an independent system of identities in V iff no w ∈ S is a consequence of S \ {w} modulo V. API lemma IsIndependent.mono (subsets of independent systems are independent) and test isIndependent_empty included.

blocks.name: IsIndependent
blocks.text:
/-- A set of words `S` is an *independent system of identities in `V`* if no `w ∈ S` is a
consequence of the remaining words `S \ {w}` modulo `V`. -/
def IsIndependent (V : GroupVariety) (S : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) : Prop :=
  ∀ w ∈ S, ¬ V.IsConsequence (S \ {w}) w

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsIndependent.mono {V : GroupVariety} {S T : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)} (hST : S ⊆ T)
    (hT : V.IsIndependent T) : V.IsIndependent S := by
  intro w hw h
  refine hT w (hST hw) fun G _ hG hS => h G hG fun s hs => ?_
  exact hS s ⟨hST hs.1, hs.2⟩

blocks.code:
def HasMinConditionOnSubvarieties (V : GroupVariety) : Prop :=
  WellFoundedLT (Set.Iic V)
blocks.docstring:
Property 1) of Problem 8.19: `V` satisfies the *minimum condition for subvarieties*, i.e.
every nonempty set of subvarieties of `V` has a minimal element (equivalently, there is no
infinite strictly descending chain of subvarieties of `V`).

blocks.code:
def HasNoInfiniteIndependentSystem (V : GroupVariety) : Prop :=
  ¬ ∃ S : Set (FreeGroup ℕ), S.Infinite ∧ V.IsIndependent S
blocks.docstring:
Property 3) of Problem 8.19: `V` has no infinite independent system of identities, i.e.
there is no infinite set of words that is independent in `V`.
blocks.name: HasNoInfiniteIndependentSystem

there is no infinite set of words that is independent in `V`. -/
def HasNoInfiniteIndependentSystem (V : GroupVariety) : Prop :=
  ¬ ∃ S : Set (FreeGroup ℕ), S.Infinite ∧ V.IsIndependent S

claims.decomposer_note: Yes/no question: for every variety of groups V, does 'V satisfies the minimum condition (no infinite strictly descending chain) on subvarieties' hold iff 'V has at most countably many subvarieties'; the direction 1)⇒2) is standard (min condition ⇔ every subvariety finitely based relative to V), so the content is the converse, but the Prop is the equivalence as posed.
claims.reviewer_why: answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ V : GroupVariety, (WellFoundedLT (Set.Iic V) ↔ (Set.Iic V).Countable). Varieties are law-defined classes of groups in Type ordered by inclusion (the lattice is the true lattice of varieties, since a variety is determined by its countable-rank relatively free group, which lives in Type). WellFoundedLT of the subtype order is the minimum condition (checked by scratch proof that it yields minimal elements); Set.Countable is 'at most countable'. All 8 candidates were equivalent here; c02 chosen for repository naming, documented property definitions and API/test lemmas.

decomposition_objections.text: Minor: the note on parts.iii says 'neither direction is known'. Under the (required) relative reading of independence, 2) ⇒ 3) is immediate: an infinite independent system S in V yields pairwise distinct subvarieties V ∧ var(T) for all T ⊆ S, hence 2^ℵ₀ subvarieties. Likewise 1) ⇒ 2) and 1) ⇒ 3) are standard, so the open content is 3) ⇒ 1) (which implies 2) ⇒ 1) and 3) ⇒ 2)). This does not affect the formalization, which states each pairwise equivalence exactly as posed.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.19

by Yu. G. Kleiman

Which of the following properties of (soluble) varieties of groups are equivalent to one
another:

1) to satisfy the minimum condition for subvarieties;

2) to have at most countably many subvarieties;

3) to have no infinite independent system of identities?

An *identity* (law) is a word $w$ in the free group on the variables $x_0, x_1, \dots$; a group
$G$ *satisfies* $w$ if $w$ evaluates to $1$ under every substitution of elements of $G$ for the
variables. A *variety of groups* is the class of all groups satisfying a given set of
identities, and a *subvariety* of a variety $\mathfrak{V}$ is a variety contained in
$\mathfrak{V}$. A set $S$ of identities is *independent in* $\mathfrak{V}$ if no $w \in S$ is a
consequence of $S \setminus \{w\}$ modulo the identities of $\mathfrak{V}$, i.e. for every
$w \in S$ some group in $\mathfrak{V}$ satisfies all identities of $S \setminus \{w\}$ but
not $w$. A variety is *soluble* if all of its groups are soluble.

Every variety is determined by its groups of countable cardinality (it is determined by its
relatively free group of countable rank), so here a variety is recorded by the class of its
groups in `Type`.

The question is split into the three pairwise equivalences 1) ⇔ 2), 1) ⇔ 3) and 2) ⇔ 3),
each asked for all varieties of groups and, as a variant, for all soluble varieties of groups.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.19»

/-- A word `w` in the free group on the variables `x₀, x₁, …` is a *law* (identity) of the
group `G` if it evaluates to `1` under every substitution of elements of `G` for the
variables. -/
def IsLaw (w : FreeGroup ℕ) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f w = 1

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isLaw_one (G : Type*) [Group G] : IsLaw 1 G :=
  fun _ => map_one _

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isLaw_of_subsingleton (w : FreeGroup ℕ) (G : Type*) [Group G] [Subsingleton G] :
    IsLaw w G :=
  fun _ => Subsingleton.elim _ _

/-- A *variety of groups*: the class of all groups satisfying some set of laws. -/
structure GroupVariety where
  /-- The groups belonging to the variety. -/
  Mem : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop
  /-- The variety is the class of all groups satisfying some set `W` of laws. -/
  exists_laws :
    ∃ W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ), ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Mem G ↔ ∀ w ∈ W, IsLaw w G

namespace GroupVariety

/-- Varieties are ordered by inclusion: `U ≤ V` means that `U` is a subvariety of `V`. -/
instance : PartialOrder GroupVariety where
  le U V := ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], U.Mem G → V.Mem G
  le_refl _ _ _ := id
  le_trans _ _ _ h₁ h₂ G _ hG := h₂ G (h₁ G hG)
  le_antisymm U V h₁ h₂ := by
    cases U
    cases V
    congr
    funext G _
    exact propext ⟨h₁ G, h₂ G⟩

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem le_def (U V : GroupVariety) : U ≤ V ↔ ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], U.Mem G → V.Mem G :=
  Iff.rfl

/-- The variety of all groups. -/
instance : OrderTop GroupVariety where
  top := { Mem := fun _ _ => True, exists_laws := ⟨∅, fun _ _ => by simp⟩ }
  le_top _ _ _ _ := trivial

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem mem_of_subsingleton (V : GroupVariety) (G : Type) [Group G] [Subsingleton G] :
    V.Mem G := by
  obtain ⟨W, hW⟩ := V.exists_laws
  exact (hW G).2 fun w _ => isLaw_of_subsingleton w G

/-- The word `w` is a *consequence of `S` modulo `V`*: every group in `V` in which all words
of `S` are laws also has `w` as a law. -/
def IsConsequence (V : GroupVariety) (S : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (w : FreeGroup ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], V.Mem G → (∀ s ∈ S, IsLaw s G) → IsLaw w G

/-- A set of words `S` is an *independent system of identities in `V`* if no `w ∈ S` is a
consequence of the remaining words `S \ {w}` modulo `V`. -/
def IsIndependent (V : GroupVariety) (S : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) : Prop :=
  ∀ w ∈ S, ¬ V.IsConsequence (S \ {w}) w

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isIndependent_empty (V : GroupVariety) : V.IsIndependent ∅ :=
  fun _ hw => hw.elim

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsIndependent.mono {V : GroupVariety} {S T : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)} (hST : S ⊆ T)
    (hT : V.IsIndependent T) : V.IsIndependent S := by
  intro w hw h
  refine hT w (hST hw) fun G _ hG hS => h G hG fun s hs => ?_
  exact hS s ⟨hST hs.1, hs.2⟩

/-- Property 1) of Problem 8.19: `V` satisfies the *minimum condition for subvarieties*, i.e.
every nonempty set of subvarieties of `V` has a minimal element (equivalently, there is no
infinite strictly descending chain of subvarieties of `V`). -/
def HasMinConditionOnSubvarieties (V : GroupVariety) : Prop :=
  WellFoundedLT (Set.Iic V)

/-- Property 2) of Problem 8.19: `V` has at most countably many subvarieties. -/
def HasCountablyManySubvarieties (V : GroupVariety) : Prop :=
  (Set.Iic V).Countable

/-- Property 3) of Problem 8.19: `V` has no infinite independent system of identities, i.e.
there is no infinite set of words that is independent in `V`. -/
def HasNoInfiniteIndependentSystem (V : GroupVariety) : Prop :=
  ¬ ∃ S : Set (FreeGroup ℕ), S.Infinite ∧ V.IsIndependent S

/-- A variety of groups is *soluble* if all of its groups are soluble. -/
def IsSoluble (V : GroupVariety) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], V.Mem G → IsSolvable G

end GroupVariety

/-- Problem 8.19, properties 1) and 2): does a variety of groups satisfy the minimum condition
for subvarieties if and only if it has at most countably many subvarieties? -/
@[category research open, AMS 8 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.19».parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ V : GroupVariety,
      (V.HasMinConditionOnSubvarieties ↔ V.HasCountablyManySubvarieties) := by
  sorry

/-- Problem 8.19, properties 1) and 3): does a variety of groups satisfy the minimum condition
for subvarieties if and only if it has no infinite independent system of identities? -/
@[category research open, AMS 8 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.19».parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ V : GroupVariety,
      (V.HasMinConditionOnSubvarieties ↔ V.HasNoInfiniteIndependentSystem) := by
  sorry

/-- Problem 8.19, properties 2) and 3): does a variety of groups have at most countably many
subvarieties if and only if it has no infinite independent system of identities? -/
@[category research open, AMS 8 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.19».parts.iii : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ V : GroupVariety,
      (V.HasCountablyManySubvarieties ↔ V.HasNoInfiniteIndependentSystem) := by
  sorry

/-- Problem 8.19 for soluble varieties, properties 1) and 2): does a soluble variety of groups
satisfy the minimum condition for subvarieties if and only if it has at most countably many
subvarieties? -/
@[category research open, AMS 8 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.19».variants.soluble.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ V : GroupVariety, V.IsSoluble →
      (V.HasMinConditionOnSubvarieties ↔ V.HasCountablyManySubvarieties) := by
  sorry

/-- Problem 8.19 for soluble varieties, properties 1) and 3): does a soluble variety of groups
satisfy the minimum condition for subvarieties if and only if it has no infinite independent
system of identities? -/
@[category research open, AMS 8 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.19».variants.soluble.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ V : GroupVariety, V.IsSoluble →
      (V.HasMinConditionOnSubvarieties ↔ V.HasNoInfiniteIndependentSystem) := by
  sorry

/-- Problem 8.19 for soluble varieties, properties 2) and 3): does a soluble variety of groups
have at most countably many subvarieties if and only if it has no infinite independent system
of identities? -/
@[category research open, AMS 8 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.19».variants.soluble.parts.iii : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ V : GroupVariety, V.IsSoluble →
      (V.HasCountablyManySubvarieties ↔ V.HasNoInfiniteIndependentSystem) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.19»

items: A variety of groups is represented by the class of its members in universe `Type` (Type 0): `Mem : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop` together with `∃ W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ), ∀ G, Mem G ↔ ∀ w ∈ W, IsLaw w G`. This loses nothing: a variety is determined by its relatively free group of countable rank, which lives in Type 0, so the lattice of these objects is isomorphic to the lattice of varieties of groups, and 'w follows from S modulo V' quantified over Type-0 groups agrees with the usual (syntactic) consequence relation.
Identities are words in `FreeGroup ℕ` (countably many variables x₀, x₁, …), the standard setting; an identity u = v corresponds to the word u v⁻¹.

'Independent system of identities' is read relative to V (as the decomposition notes require): S is independent in V iff no w ∈ S is a consequence of (S \ {w}) together with the laws of V. This is the only reading under which the three properties are comparable; the absolute reading (independent subsets of the laws of V, or independent bases of V) would concern supervarieties and make 1) ⇔ 3) trivially false.

'Minimum condition for subvarieties' is formalized as `WellFoundedLT (Set.Iic V)` (every nonempty set of subvarieties has a minimal element; classically equivalent to the absence of infinite strictly descending chains). Subvarieties of V are `Set.Iic V`, which includes V itself and the trivial variety.
'At most countably many subvarieties' is `(Set.Iic V).Countable` (finite or countably infinite).

'Infinite independent system' uses `Set.Infinite`; since FreeGroup ℕ is countable this is the same as countably infinite, and subsets of independent systems are independent (proved as `IsIndependent.mono`).
A soluble variety is one all of whose groups are soluble (`IsSolvable`); this is equivalent to being a subvariety of some 𝔄^n.

Because the deliverable is a single problem file, the reusable definitions (IsLaw, GroupVariety, …) are placed in the problem file rather than in FormalConjecturesForMathlib; a reviewer may wish to move them. AMS tags used: 8 (general algebraic systems / varieties) and 20 (group theory).

reviewer_notes: All eight candidates formalized all six slots and all are mathematically faithful under the same (only sensible) reading: 'independent system of identities' is taken relative to V (a set of words none of which follows, modulo the laws of V, from the others). The absolute reading (independent subsets of the laws of V) would make 1)⇔3) trivially false since the trivial variety's laws contain infinite independent sets (Vaughan-Lee/Ol'shanskii). Modelling choices: words in FreeGroup ℕ (w = 1); varieties as law-defined classes of Type-0 groups (c01/c02/c08; c03 universe-polymorphic) or as semantically closed law sets (c04–c07) — both give exactly the lattice of varieties, since fully invariant subgroups of FreeGroup ℕ are exactly the semantically closed sets and F_∞/N ∈ Type. Min condition: WellFoundedLT on Set.Iic V (classically equivalent to no infinite strictly descending chain, which c03/c05/c06 use directly). Solubility: 'every group soluble' (c01–c05,c08) vs uniform derived-length bound (c06,c07) are equivalent. c02 chosen as the final file verbatim (compiles with only sorry warnings): it follows the repository's kourovka.«8.19».parts.i naming (c05–c07 use bare parts.i), documents each property as a named definition, and provides API/test lemmas for the bespoke definitions. Note on the decomposition table: the note on parts.iii says 'neither direction is known', but under the required relative reading 2)⇒3) is immediate (an infinite independent system S yields 2^|S| distinct subvarieties V ∧ var(T), T ⊆ S); the open content is 3)⇒1). This does not affect the formalization, which states each pairwise equivalence as posed. Residual uncertainty is only about whether Kleiman intended some other notion of 'independent system'; the relative reading is the one consistent with the problem being non-trivial and with the decomposition notes.

statement_segments.text: Which of the following properties of (soluble) varieties of groups are equivalent to one another

statement_tex:
Which of the following properties of (soluble)
varieties of groups are equivalent to one another:

 \makebox[15pt][r]{}1) to satisfy the minimum condition for
subvarieties;

 \makebox[15pt][r]{}2) to have at most countably
many subvarieties;

 \makebox[15pt][r]{}3) to have no infinite independent system of
identities?
title: Conjecture 8.19
